enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
425 PM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 421 PM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

 - Isolated thunderstorms will move into SW New Mexico this
   afternoon and early evening.

 - Rain showers will increase in coverage across the area this
   evening into Saturday morning, and linger east of the Rio
   Grande on Saturday. A few snow flakes could mix in at the
   highest elevations of the Sacramento Mountains, with no
   accumulation.

 - Very cool temperatures will accompany the rain and clouds, 
   with highs running 10 to 15 degrees below normal on Saturday.

 - Temperatures will return to near normal by the middle of next 
   week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 233 PM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

Upper level system is on tract, with a closed low dropping south
along the Lower Colorado River Valley, and increasing moisture and
diffluence aloft. 

A few thunderstorms over Cochise County, AZ will likely work into
parts of Hidalgo County, NM in the next hour or two. Otherwise,
expect showers to become light to moderate as they increase in
coverage across the area, especially after dark.

NBM/ForeastBuilder tried to produce a bit too much rain/snow mix
over the Sacramento Mountains. Expect nearly-saturated conditions
and a cold rain late tonight into Saturday, with accumulating snow
levels above 10-11K feet, and brief mixing down to around 9000 
feet, with no impacts. Most areas will see beneficial rainfall
amounts of around 0.10 to 0.25 inches from this system, and a few
pockets over 0.50 inches, mainly east of El Paso.

Tomorrow will be soup or stew weather over ELP and LRU. Cloudy, 
showery, and damp, with highs stuck in the upper-50s in the
lowlands, and upper-30s in the Sacramentos. 

Quieter weather overall next week, though a disorganized trough
will skirt the area Tuesday night, with a spotty shower or two not
out of the question. Otherwise, expect slowly warming
temperatures, back to near normal (lower-70s in the lowlands) by
Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 421 PM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

Rain showers moving in from the Arizona-New Mexico state line
could cause visibilities to drop to MVFR levels at some points 
during the night, but otherwise, conditions will generally be VFR.
Winds will continue to prevail from the east at 8-12 kt. Skies
will mainly be OVC as the day progresses and the rain showers 
continue, some temporary bouts of moderate rain are possible in 
the overnight hours.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 233 PM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

An upper level disturbance will bring widespread clouds, and light 
to moderate rain showers to the wider region through Saturday. Rain
will linger the longest near and east of the Rio Grande on Saturday,
but most areas will see wetting rainfall. Temperatures will be held
back well below normal, with highs in the upper-30s above 8000 feet.
and much of the lowlands stuck in the upper-50s and lower-60s. This
will be about 10 to 15 degrees below normal. A few snow flakes could
briefly mix in at the highest elevations.

Vent rates will generally be poor, except in SW New Mexico in the
afternoon. Less favorable vent rates will be a challenge until mid
week when deeper mixing and warmer temperatures arrive.

&&
